inlines.text: Calculate the surface area of this triangular prism.

answer.short: Front and back: $60\text{ cm}^2$; left side: $96\text{ cm}^2$; right side: $104\text{ cm}^2$; bottom: $40\text{ cm}^2$; total: $300\text{ cm}^2$.
answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}A_{\text{front and back}}&=\frac{5\times12}{2}\times2\\&=60\text{ cm}^2\\A_{\text{left side}}&=8\times12\\&=96\text{ cm}^2\\A_{\text{right side}}&=8\times13\\&=104\text{ cm}^2\\A_{\text{bottom}}&=8\times5\\&=40\text{ cm}^2\\A_{\text{total}}&=60+96+104+40\\&=300\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$

answer.worked:
Area of ends:	$(8\times5-3\times2)\times2=68$
Area of outside:	$(8\times12)\times2+(5\times12)\times2=312$
Area of inside:	$(3\times12)\times2+(2\times12)\times2=120$
$$\begin{align*}A&=68+312+120\\A&=500\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$

Area of ends:	$(10\times10-\pi(2)^2)\times2=200-8\pi$
Area of outside:	$(10\times10)\times4=400$
Area of inside:	$2\pi(2)(10)=40\pi$
$$\begin{align*}A&=200-8\pi+400+40\pi\\A&=600+32\pi\\A&\approx700.5\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$

A **net** is a flat, connected arrangement of all the faces of a 3D shape that folds to make the shape.

A **prism** is a solid with two identical, parallel end faces joined by rectangular faces.

The **surface area** of a prism is the total area of all its faces.

It equals the area of the prism's net.

The [[surface area|34]] of a prism is the total area of all its faces.
To calculate it, add the areas of all of the [[faces|20]].

To find the surface area, picture the faces covering the 3D shape.

This avoids drawing the net.
A cylinder's net has two identical circles and one rectangle. The rectangle's length equals the circumference of a circle, and its width equals the height of the cylinder.
$2\pi r^2$ represents the [[area of the two circular ends|59]]
$2\pi rh$ represents the [[area of the curved surface|61]]
The rectangle's dimensions are the cylinder's height and the [[circumference|38]] of its circular ends.

- Some questions ask for the surface area of a part of a cylinder.
- Adjust the formula by asking:
  - Is there a full circular end, part of an end, or no end?
  - How much of the curved surface remains?
- Is there a new flat surface where the cylinder was "cut"?
